adaptive.difficulty_levers: path length, forward vs reverse, pad spacing and density, presentation speed, optional retention delay
adaptive.notes: Paths are procedurally generated and length is a native staircase, giving matched parallel routes.

engagement_hook: Guide a lost firefly home by walking its glowing trail backwards; longer trails feel like braver journeys.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Motor/device: mis-taps on close pads are mitigated by large, well-spaced targets and tap-not-drag. Attention/ADHD: impulsive tapping inflates errors, so error types are separated and engagement is gated before tail calls. Familiarity: reverse-retrace self-teaches via the ghost-hand and warm-up. Strategy learning: reversing a path can be partly strategic, so path and efficiency are reported alongside pure span.

name: Mobile Stash (nonverbal complex span)
one_liner: The child answers a quick nonverbal puzzle (which side of the beam tips? is it symmetric? which way does the piece point?) then remembers a charm hung on a mobile; after several cycles taps the charms back in order.
interaction: Each cycle shows a processing puzzle answered with a two-choice tap - toggle among BALANCE (which side of the beam tips, or is it level: a nonverbal operation), SYMMETRY (is the hanging pattern mirror-symmetric), ROTATE (which upright direction the tilted charm points) and COUNT (how many charms of a target kind) - then briefly hangs a coloured charm at a position to remember. After N cycles the child taps the charms back in presentation order. Set size rises when recall is perfect AND processing stayed accurate, falls otherwise; processing is time-limited so it cannot be skipped.
self_teach: The ghost-hand taps the heavier side of a beam, a charm appears, it does one more cycle, then taps the two charms back in order with a check mark (about 9s); one unscored warm-up follows. Icons (scale, mirror, curved arrow, tally) show the current puzzle with no text.

learning_science.why: Complex span (interleaving processing and storage) predicts fluid intelligence because it taxes attention control, not just storage.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Interleave a nonverbal processing judgment with spatial storage and score the recalled span.
learning_science.source: Engle, R. W. (2002). Working memory capacity as executive attention. Current Directions in Psychological Science, 11(1), 19-23.

learning_science.why: Symmetry and other visuospatial complex spans are reliable, largely language-free capacity measures.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Anchor young and low-literacy bands with the symmetry and balance modules and spatial charm storage.
learning_science.source: Kane, M. J., Hambrick, D. Z., Tuholski, S. W., Wilhelm, O., Payne, T. W., & Engle, R. W. (2004). The generality of working memory capacity. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 133(2), 189-217.

learning_science.why: A storage span is valid only if the child actually performs the processing task rather than trading it away.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Enforce a processing-accuracy gate (at least 80%) before crediting a storage span.
learning_science.source: Conway, A. R. A., Kane, M. J., Bunting, M. F., Hambrick, D. Z., Wilhelm, O., & Engle, R. W. (2005). Working memory span tasks: A methodological review and user's guide. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 12(5), 769-786.

tail_precision_rationale: Interleaving a nonverbal judgment with spatial storage taxes attention control, not storage alone: the adaptive recall span (M-SPAN, M-DIFFREACH) is a continuous above-grade capacity index, position partial-credit (M-POLY) extracts graded tail signal, and processing accuracy (M-PROCACC) gates the storage score so children who neglect the puzzle to inflate recall are flagged; error typing (M-ERRTYPE), cross-form consistency (M-CONSIST) and low processing-task RT variability (M-RTVAR) mark secure high-capacity solvers rather than fast guessers.
age_rationale: Dual-tasking with a secondary judgment overloads most K-1 executive control, so the floor is 2-3 using the simplest balance or symmetry module at set size 2; rotation, counting and larger sets suit 4-5 and 6-8, and the reading module is age-gated to 4-5 and up. Responses are taps only.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 balance/symmetry span at set size 2 up to 6-8 rotation/operation span at set sizes 4-5 with an optional reading module
adaptive.difficulty_levers: set size, processing module and its difficulty/time limit, processing-storage similarity, charm-position density
adaptive.notes: Processing items and charm layouts are generated and set size is a native staircase; the processing-accuracy gate must be enforced for a valid span.

engagement_hook: A hanging-mobile balancing game where you solve a quick puzzle then stash a charm, proving you can juggle thinking and remembering at once.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Academic skill: operation and reading modules confound with math and literacy, so young or low-literacy children use the balance, symmetry and rotation modules and processing accuracy is reported separately. Attention/ADHD: dual-tasking amplifies attention effects, so gate on M-PROCACC and engagement. Speed-accuracy trade-off on processing is caught by M-PROCACC. Colour vision: charms use distinct hues plus shape redundancy. Motor/familiarity: large targets and a warm-up.

name: Recipe Recall (verbal/numeric complex span)
one_liner: Between remembering each ingredient the child answers a quick check (does this step make sense? is this measurement right?), then recalls the ingredients in order or in reverse - a verbal/numeric complex span.
interaction: Each cycle shows a processing check answered true/false - toggle among READ (does a short pictured or spoken step make sense), OPERATION (is a simple measurement right, e.g. 2 cups plus 1 cup makes 3 cups), COUNT (is the tally correct) and SYMMETRY/ROTATE (is the plating mirrored, or which way the utensil points) - then briefly shows an ingredient to remember. After N cycles the child taps the ingredients back in presentation order, with a Reverse-recall toggle that asks for them in reverse (a backward span under load). Set size adapts up on perfect recall with accurate processing; processing is time-limited.
self_teach: The ghost-hand marks a sensible step true, an ingredient appears, one more cycle follows, then it taps the two ingredients back in order with a check mark (about 9s); one unscored warm-up follows. A large check and cross plus the ingredient tray teach the rhythm with no reading required in the demo.

learning_science.principle: Reading span and the processing-storage trade-off
learning_science.why: Interleaving comprehension with storage is the classic complex-span predictor of higher-order verbal ability.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a sensibility judgment as the processing task while holding ingredients for ordered recall.
learning_science.source: Daneman, M., & Carpenter, P. A. (1980). Individual differences in working memory and reading. Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior, 19(4), 450-466.

learning_science.why: Standardized operation span (verify a simple computation plus storage) is a reliable individual-difference measure of WM capacity.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Offer an operation module (verify a simple measurement) as an alternate processing task.
learning_science.source: Unsworth, N., Heitz, R. P., Schrock, J. C., & Engle, R. W. (2005). An automated version of the operation span task. Behavior Research Methods, 37(3), 498-505.

learning_science.why: Recalling the held set in reverse taxes manipulation beyond storage, lifting the ceiling for older children.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Add a reverse-recall toggle so the same shell yields a manipulation contrast (backward digit span under load).
learning_science.source: Baddeley, A. D., & Hitch, G. (1974). Working memory. In G. H. Bower (Ed.), The Psychology of Learning and Motivation (Vol. 8, pp. 47-89). Academic Press.

tail_precision_rationale: A verbal or numeric processing task interleaved with ordered storage indexes executive attention: adaptive recall span (M-SPAN, M-DIFFREACH) is an above-grade capacity index, position partial-credit (M-POLY) grades each recall, processing accuracy (M-PROCACC) gates validity against speed-accuracy trade-offs, and intrusion-lure typing (M-LURETYPE) with order-vs-item error typing (M-ERRTYPE) exposes proactive-interference control; the reverse-recall toggle adds a manipulation contrast that lifts the ceiling, while first-move latency (M-RTFIRST) is logged as process only.
age_rationale: The reading and operation modules require basic literacy and numeracy, so the honest floor is 4-5 (matching operation-span and backward-digit items at 4-5) and scales to reading span and reverse recall at 6-8; it is not used pre-reading, so K-1 is excluded. Responses are taps only.

adaptive.content_range: 4-5 operation span at set size 2 with forward recall up to 6-8 reading span with reverse recall at set sizes 4-5
adaptive.difficulty_levers: set size, processing module and time limit, forward vs reverse recall, lure similarity of the memoranda
adaptive.notes: Processing items and memoranda are generated and set size is a native staircase; the processing-accuracy gate must be enforced.

engagement_hook: A cooking-line game where you fact-check each step then remember the ingredients in order, like keeping a busy recipe straight in your head.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Academic skill: reading and operation modules confound with literacy and numeracy, so processing accuracy is reported separately and the type is reserved for 4-5 and up. Attention/ADHD: dual-tasking amplifies attention, so gate on M-PROCACC and engagement. Speed-accuracy trade-off is detected by M-PROCACC. Motor/familiarity: large tray targets and a warm-up. Language: spoken steps have picture equivalents so the demo is reading-free.

name: Signal Radar (dual n-back / updating)
one_liner: Blips sweep a radar scope while tones or letters play, and the child flags when the current position (or sound) matches the one n sweeps back, or keeps a running value or tally that must be updated.
interaction: In n-back mode a blip appears on the scope each sweep and the child taps WHERE-MATCH when the current position equals the one n sweeps back; dual mode adds a letter channel with a separate WHAT-MATCH button and the child responds to either channel. A numeric-updating shell shows a running value changed by occasional operations and probes the current value; a symbol-counter shell requires separate running tallies of two or more blip types, reported on demand. Responses do not advance the sweep; n or update load rises at high sensitivity and falls at low.
self_teach: A wordless 1-back demo shows two blips in the same spot one sweep apart and the hand tapping WHERE-MATCH with a check mark (about 7s), then an unscored 1-back warm-up; the sweep rhythm and the match button read instantly with no text.

learning_science.principle: N-back as a continuous updating measure
learning_science.why: The n-back requires constant encoding, monitoring and replacement of WM contents and correlates with fluid reasoning.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Use a continuous sweep with a MATCH judgment and an adaptive n level.
learning_science.source: Kirchner, W. K. (1958). Age differences in short-term retention of rapidly changing information. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 55(4), 352-358.

learning_science.why: Adding a second modality stream increases domain-general updating demand and lifts the ceiling for older children.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Provide a dual spatial-plus-verbal mode with separate response buttons per channel.
learning_science.source: Jaeggi, S. M., Buschkuehl, M., Jonides, J., & Perrig, W. J. (2008). Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 105(19), 6829-6833.

learning_science.why: Hits and false alarms confound ability with response bias unless modeled with sensitivity.
learning_science.concrete_decision: Score with d-prime and flag lure false alarms rather than raw hit counts.
learning_science.source: Green, D. M., & Swets, J. A. (1966). Signal Detection Theory and Psychophysics. Wiley.

tail_precision_rationale: A continuous dual-channel updating task is rich in process telemetry: signal-detection sensitivity (M-DPRIME) separates true match detection from response bias, the highest sustained n and update load (M-DIFFREACH) probe capacity above grade level, lure (n plus or minus 1) false alarms (M-ERRTYPE) reveal fragile temporal binding, the accuracy-by-load slope (M-UPDATECOST) indexes updating efficiency, and RT variability and lapses (M-RTVAR, M-LAPSE) with drift and engagement gating (M-DRIFT, M-ENGAGE) score worst-performance consistency rather than impulsive speed.
age_rationale: Continuous updating with response withholding is too demanding and attention-confounded for most K-1 children, so the floor is 2-3 (single 1-back), moving to 2-back and numeric updating at 4-5 and 2-3-back, dual-channel and multi-counter shells at 6-8. Only one or two large buttons are tapped, and the numeric and counter shells assume counting so they are age-gated to 4-5 and up.

adaptive.content_range: 2-3 single 1-back up to 6-8 dual (spatial plus verbal) n-back, numeric running-value and multi-symbol-counter updating
adaptive.difficulty_levers: n level, single vs dual channel, sweep pace, target and lure rate, update step size, number of counters
adaptive.notes: Sweeps, tones, operations and probe schedules are generated with controlled target and lure rates, and n and update load are native staircases.

engagement_hook: A sonar-scope arcade where you flag repeating blips and keep the count straight; speeding sweeps and dual channels make leveling up feel like manning mission control.
construct_irrelevant_risks: Attention/ADHD is the dominant confound: continuous updating loads sustained attention and impulse control, so d-prime (bias-free) is reported, drift and engagement are tracked across the sweep, consistency is weighted over speed, and scores are gated on engaged blocks. Numeracy: numeric and counter shells need counting and are age-gated. Motor: a fixed sweep may clip slow responses, mitigated by a generous response window. Familiarity: novelty is mitigated by the warm-up. Audio: the WHAT channel uses visible letters so audio is not required.
